[short] skip 'runs test'

env BOLERO_MODULE=on

# Issue 35837: "bolero vet -<analyzer> <std package>" should use the requested
# analyzers, not the default analyzers for 'bolero test'.
bolero vet -n -buildtags=false runtime
stderr '-buildtags=false'
! stderr '-unsafeptr=false'

# Issue 37030: "bolero vet <std package>" without other flags should disable the
# unsafeptr check by default.
bolero vet -n runtime
stderr '-unsafeptr=false'
! stderr '-unreachable=false'

# However, it should be enabled if requested explicitly.
bolero vet -n -unsafeptr runtime
stderr '-unsafeptr'
! stderr '-unsafeptr=false'

# -unreachable is disabled during test but on during plain vet.
# The -a makes sure the vet result is not cached, or else we won't print the command line.
bolero test -a -n runtime
stderr '-unreachable=false'

# A flag terminator should be allowed before the package list.
bolero vet -n -- .

[short] stop

# Analyzer flags should be included from BOLERO_FLAGS, and should override
# the defaults.
bolero vet .
env BOLERO_FLAGS='-tags=buggy'
! bolero vet .
stderr 'possible Printf formatting directive'

# Enabling one analyzer in BOLERO_FLAGS should disable the rest implicitly...
env BOLERO_FLAGS='-tags=buggy -unsafeptr'
bolero vet .

# ...but enabling one on the command line should not disable the analyzers
# enabled via BOLERO_FLAGS.
env BOLERO_FLAGS='-tags=buggy -printf'
! bolero vet -unsafeptr
stderr 'possible Printf formatting directive'

# Analyzer flags don't exist unless we're running 'bolero vet',
# and we shouldn't run the vet tool to discover them otherwise.
# (Maybe someday we'll hard-code the analyzer flags for the default vet
# tool to make this work, but not right now.)
env BOLERO_FLAGS='-unsafeptr'
! bolero list .
stderr 'bolero: parsing \$BOLERO_FLAGS: unknown flag -unsafeptr'
env BOLERO_FLAGS=

# "bolero test" on a user package should by default enable an explicit list of analyzers.
bolero test -n -run=none .
stderr '[/\\]vet'$GOEXE'["]? .* -errorsas .* ["]?\$WORK[/\\][^ ]*[/\\]vet\.cfg'

# An explicitly-empty -vet argument should imply the default analyzers.
bolero test -n -vet= -run=none .
stderr '[/\\]vet'$GOEXE'["]? .* -errorsas .* ["]?\$WORK[/\\][^ ]*[/\\]vet\.cfg'

# "bolero test" on a standard package should by default disable an explicit list.
bolero test -a -n -run=none encoding/binary
stderr '[/\\]vet'$GOEXE'["]? -unsafeptr=false -unreachable=false ["]?\$WORK[/\\][^ ]*[/\\]vet\.cfg'

bolero test -a -n -vet= -run=none encoding/binary
stderr '[/\\]vet'$GOEXE'["]? -unsafeptr=false -unreachable=false ["]?\$WORK[/\\][^ ]*[/\\]vet\.cfg'

# Both should allow users to override via the -vet flag.
bolero test -a -n -vet=unreachable -run=none .
stderr '[/\\]vet'$GOEXE'["]? -unreachable ["]?\$WORK[/\\][^ ]*[/\\]vet\.cfg'
bolero test -a -n -vet=unreachable -run=none encoding/binary
stderr '[/\\]vet'$GOEXE'["]? -unreachable ["]?\$WORK[/\\][^ ]*[/\\]vet\.cfg'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/x
-- x.go --
package x
-- x_test.go --
package x
-- x_tagged.go --
// +build buggy

package x

import "fmt"

func init() {
	fmt.Sprint("%s") // oops!
}
